section_1_presentation_and_advisory.name: Strategic Delivery & Value Articulation
section_1_presentation_and_advisory.focus: Can they connect technical architecture to business value? Can they clearly articulate why they built this solution and how it handles commercial reality?
section_1_presentation_and_advisory.criteria: Delivers a compelling, narrative-driven walkthrough of the user experience framed around customer personas and operational impact. Explicitly justifies why the architecture directly solves the root business problem (avoiding a 'science project') and presents a viable Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) model that demonstrates fiscal responsibility.
section_1_presentation_and_advisory.score_3_expert_criteria: Quantifies unit economics ($/1k queries, BigQuery scan cost per SKU lookup, Cloud Run CPU/memory second billing vs provisioned vector cluster baseline), ties latency and citation accuracy directly to retail conversion/cart-abandonment KPIs, and models sensitivity under 10x traffic burst.
score_3_disqualifiers: Qualitative cost claims without per-query or monthly dollar math
Missing comparison against alternative architectures (e.g. provisioned Vector DB or unconstrained Text-to-SQL)
No explicit mapping between technical SLAs and retail business KPIs

section_1_presentation_and_advisory.name: Objection Handling & Technical Defense
section_1_presentation_and_advisory.focus: How do they react to executive pushback, and can they programmatically defend their implementation choices?
section_1_presentation_and_advisory.criteria: Remains entirely calm, collected, and collaborative under pressure when facing stakeholder resistance. Confidently defends engineering decisions and structural design choices during the Q&A matrix using data-backed logic, while cleanly evaluating and addressing technical trade-offs (e.g., cost vs. latency, model tiering).
section_1_presentation_and_advisory.score_3_expert_criteria: Preempts CISO, CTO, and CFO objections with empirical benchmark data (measured p95 latency breakdown, adversarial jailbreak rejection rates, SQL injection vs prompt injection separation) and explicitly documents where current design trade-offs break down at scale.
score_3_disqualifiers: Claims architecture has zero weaknesses or trade-offs
Defends choices with buzzwords rather than measured latency/accuracy/cost numbers
Conflates database query parameterization with LLM prompt security

section_1_presentation_and_advisory.name: Presentation Skills & Time Management
section_1_presentation_and_advisory.focus: How effectively do they manage time, pacing, and the overall flow of the meeting?
section_1_presentation_and_advisory.criteria: Paces the presentation to finish on time. Tactfully steers the panel away from rabbit holes, offering to take tangential topics offline without being dismissive. Demonstrates intellectual honesty by confidently admitting 'I don't know, but I will get back to you' rather than fabricating answers.
section_1_presentation_and_advisory.score_3_expert_criteria: Provides a structured 5-8 slide executive narrative with explicit time-boxed agendas, demo scripts anchored to verifiable SKUs, and a parking-lot matrix for out-of-scope enterprise integrations (ERP, real-time inventory locking).
score_3_disqualifiers: No structured slide-by-slide executive walkthrough or demo runbook
Fails to explicitly define out-of-scope boundaries to deflect rabbit holes

section_1_presentation_and_advisory.name: AI Driven Development Discussion
section_1_presentation_and_advisory.focus: How effectively do they demonstrate the use of GenAI tools and harness concepts to accelerate their own development lifecycle and code quality?
section_1_presentation_and_advisory.criteria: Articulates how their harness was set up before coding. Demonstrates understanding of establishing key guidance that enables both 'in the loop' (quick feature fix that adheres to spec) and 'outside the loop' (goal driven - task is taken and executed in a loop through lint, test, etc. until goal is passed) development. Incorporates mistakes by the agent/harness back into agent instructions.
section_1_presentation_and_advisory.score_3_expert_criteria: Implements a multi-agent adversarial harness (hierarchical AGENTS.md, TDD/eval hillclimbing loops, doc-sync enforcement gates, and multi-pane tmux review panels) with concrete post-mortems showing how past agent mistakes were encoded into automated guardrails.
score_3_disqualifiers: Static AGENTS.md without automated test/lint/doc-sync enforcement hooks
No closed-loop feedback mechanism showing how agent failures updated harness rules

section_1_presentation_and_advisory.name: Futures / Roadmap (GCP Value)
section_1_presentation_and_advisory.focus: Can they communicate what the next phase of development would look like while driving home the value of Google Cloud?
section_1_presentation_and_advisory.criteria: Articulates a clear, progressive roadmap for future development phases, addressing key elements like production-grade scalability, performance optimization, and features of the solution that the customer would want in production. Effectively demonstrates the strategic value of Google Cloud integration, explaining how native GCP services enhance stability, security, and long-term business value.
section_1_presentation_and_advisory.score_3_expert_criteria: Sequences concrete Phase 2/3 GCP architectural upgrades (Vertex AI Vector Search hybrid retrieval, BigQuery BI Engine / slot autoscaling, Model Armor, Cloud CDN + Global External Application Load Balancer) with migration triggers, cost impact, and latency delta estimates.
score_3_disqualifiers: Generic wishlist of GCP service names without architectural integration paths or migration triggers
No analysis of cost/complexity increases introduced by Phase 2 services

score_3_disqualifiers: Adding a new tool or product category requires rewriting core orchestrator control flow
